destination.name: Leigh Creek
destination.tagline: Gateway town to the northern Flinders, with fossils, ruins and outback art
destination.description: Leigh Creek is the gateway town to the northern Flinders Ranges, 540 km north of Adelaide. Its coalfield closed in 2015, and the dam beside it is now used for kayaking and fishing. Around it are the stone township of Beltana, the sculptures and ochre pits at Lyndhurst, and Nilpena Ediacara National Park, where guided tours reach a field of early animal fossils.

goodToKnow.title: Book Nilpena tours early
goodToKnow.detail: There is no independent access to Nilpena. Guide-led tours leave from the park entrance, and booking well ahead is recommended.

goodToKnow.title: Plan for distance
goodToKnow.detail: Sights lie tens of kilometres apart and towns are small. Carry water, spare fuel and supplies between stops.

destination.bestTimeBlurb: {months} brings cool, clear days for exploring the outback, while summers are very hot.

destination.name: Vulkathunha-Gammon Ranges National Park
destination.tagline: Rugged gorges and ranges, with ridgetop 4WD tours and a dark sky sanctuary
destination.description: Vulkathunha-Gammon Ranges National Park was proclaimed in 1970 on the traditional country of the Adnyamathanha people. Its gorge hikes and 4WD tracks cross rugged ranges, reaching the edge of Lake Frome, an ephemeral salt lake about 100 km long. Arkaroola Wilderness Sanctuary, a 610 sq km private reserve beside the park, is the main visitor base. In 2023 it was certified as South Australia's first International Dark Sky Sanctuary.

goodToKnow.title: Check which tracks need 4WD
goodToKnow.detail: Most park tracks suit 2WD, but the Wortupa Loop Track and the track to Lake Frome need a 4WD.

goodToKnow.title: Check park alerts
goodToKnow.detail: The park can close at short notice, for fire or pest control. Look at the park alerts before you drive in.

goodToKnow.title: Bring water and supplies
goodToKnow.detail: Facilities are basic: pit toilets at some campgrounds, and showers only at Balcanoona. The park is about 625 km from Adelaide.

destination.bestTimeBlurb: Visit in {months} for mild days and comfortable gorge walks, as summer heat is extreme.
